metadata.disclaimer: Strategies optimize performance but do not replace language development

entries.description: Read questions during the pause; underline keywords; predict what kind of answer is needed.
Speakers often mention wrong information before correcting themselves. The final version is the answer.
If you miss an answer, let it go and focus on the next question. Dwelling causes you to miss more.
At transfer time, check spelling and ensure answers do not exceed the word limit.

entries.purpose: Identify correct answers despite different wording
entries.description: Correct answers often use synonyms or paraphrased expressions, not exact words from the question.
Read headings, subheadings, and first sentences of paragraphs to get the gist before answering.
entries.common_mistake: Reading every word in detail first

entries.description: Allocate 15 minutes for passage 1, 20 for passage 2, 25 for passage 3 (usually most difficult).
entries.common_mistake: Spending too long on first passage

entries.description: False = text contradicts statement. Not Given = text doesn't mention it. Look for evidence.
entries.common_mistake: Marking False when answer is Not Given

entries.description: There is no penalty for wrong answers. Always guess if unsure.
Questions rarely use exact words from the passage. Look for synonyms and paraphrased expressions.
Spend 3-5 minutes planning. For Task 2, write thesis statement and paragraph topics.
Include a clear overview paragraph stating the main trend(s) or key features.
entries.common_mistake: No overview; listing all data points

entries.description: One central idea per paragraph. Begin with a topic sentence.
Leave 2-3 minutes to check for spelling, grammar, and coherence.
Examiners are trained to identify memorised responses. Always address the specific question.
entries.common_mistake: Using a memorised essay regardless of question

entries.description: In Part 1, give 2-3 sentence answers with a reason or example. Don't give one-word answers.
Use Opinion, Explanation, Example. State view, explain why, give example.
Memorised answers are detectable and penalised. Practice with varied, spontaneous prompts.
Avoid forcing idioms or advanced vocabulary. Use language naturally and flexibly.
Occasional self-correction is natural. Frequent self-correction disrupts fluency.
